pgVersion.description:
Version of PostgreSQL to use, changes the cluster naming scheme. Without a value, `global.fallbackDefaults.cnpg.pgVersion` is used, and `type: vectors` uses `16` as it has no image for PostgreSQL 18. It only applies to `operator` mode, and is ignored in `standalone` mode.

It only applies to `operator` mode, and is ignored in `standalone` mode.

Without a value, `global.fallbackDefaults.cnpg.pgVersion` is used. `type: vectors` has no image for PostgreSQL 18, so without a value it uses `16`.

:::caution[Changing the version of an existing cluster]

CloudNativePG upgrades an existing cluster in place when its major version changes, with `pg_upgrade`. This also happens when a cluster has no `pgVersion` set and the default changes, so **set `pgVersion` to keep a cluster on its current version**.

- Take a full backup first, and a new one afterwards. Older backups can't be used for point-in-time recovery across major versions.
- All instances are stopped during the upgrade, and replicas are cloned again afterwards.
- It needs CloudNativePG 1.26 or newer.
- CloudNativePG only supports this between images on the same OS distribution. The images of this version of common moved to Debian 13, so a cluster on an older image should stay on its major version through that change, and upgrade afterwards.
- Check that the extensions of the cluster can be upgraded, such as PostGIS or VectorChord.
- If the upgrade fails, set `pgVersion` back to the previous version. CloudNativePG then starts the cluster on that version again.
- Run `ANALYZE` afterwards, as `pg_upgrade` does not keep the statistics.

:::

allowRollingUpdateWithRWO.description:
Keep `strategy: RollingUpdate` on a single replica Deployment with `ReadWriteOnce` volumes, instead of changing it to `Recreate`. Can be overruled with `workload.$name.allowRollingUpdateWithRWO`. Updates can get stuck if the storage stays locked to the old pod, which can happen on the same node with storage like iSCSI, and two pods use the same data during an update.

:::caution

Enabling this applies to all workloads of the chart that set `strategy: RollingUpdate`. Common shows a warning in the notes for each of them.

:::

allowRollingUpdateWithRWO.description:
Keep `strategy: RollingUpdate` on a single replica Deployment with `ReadWriteOnce` volumes, instead of changing it to `Recreate`. Overrules `global.fallbackDefaults.allowRollingUpdateWithRWO`. `ReadWriteOncePod` volumes always use `Recreate`.

:::caution

Rolling updates with `ReadWriteOnce` storage are not safe for every app or storage:

- An update gets stuck if the storage stays locked to the old pod. This can happen on the same node with storage like iSCSI, and on another node with any `ReadWriteOnce` storage.
- Two pods use the same data during an update, which can damage data of apps that expect to be alone, for example with SQLite or database migrations.

Common shows a warning in the notes when this is enabled.

:::
